summary.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 net EBITDA margin to be better than the ~47% analyst estimate, and sees a path to at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops and ARR improves.
Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.
capex_capacity: Aurika Shimla (owned, 90 rooms): about Rs 108 crore deployed as of 30 June 2026; opening shortly as finishing and licences are in final stage.
Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.
Aurika Varanasi (leased heritage, 47 rooms): work begun; opening expected FY29.
Aurika Nehru Place Delhi: approvals pending; opening on or after FY30; DDA letter of award validity extended by one year.
Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is Keys' 19% RevPAR growth in line with the pre-renovation plan, and what remains to be spent on Keys renovation?
qa_highlights.answer: Keys is close to the Red Fox ARR target of about Rs 4,500 and is still a work in progress; management expects full performance next year with occupancy near Lemon Tree averages and reiterated a Rs 60 crore Keys EBITDA target. Remaining spend on about 300 rooms is about Rs 13-14 crore, at roughly Rs 4-5 lakh per key for second-tier Keys hotels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR grow only 2% despite Keys growth, and is the lower-ARR strategy continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the retail push to fill rooms during the West Asia-driven corporate slowdown lowered net ARR after commissions. It called this temporary, with a more balanced occupancy-ARR mix from July and August, and said Q1 was an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's Rs 2,500-3,000 crore deployment and Warburg's Rs 960 crore be done at peak-cycle prices, and what are the IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry to deploy and that it is not in an up cycle, since India occupancy is in the mid-60s versus a 70-72% up-cycle threshold. It will focus on demand-dense top 6-7 cities, nearby 3-5 hour international markets and leisure locations, using brownfield, operating assets at 6-8x, greenfield and long leases, with returns targeted at about 60% post-fees ROCE and a conservative downturn assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 and FY28 net EBITDA margins recover, given the 47% analyst estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be well above 47%. It targets at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops to about 1% of revenue and GST drag falls from about 2% of net revenue, with ARR rising 5-6% in Q2 and further in winter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mumbai guidance being cut, and will Aurika Mumbai reach double-digit RevPAR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was an aberration and that Q2 will be better, citing about 2,000 new rooms near the Mumbai airport. It said RevPAR is stabilised and the focus is now on repricing Aurika ARR, and declined to give a numerical RevPAR target before Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2,000-room opening target for FY27 slip, given 334 rooms opened in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slippage is normal in the business but it is broadly confident of about 2,000 rooms, based on the current pipeline and owner relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net room additions lag the 334 rooms opened in Q1, and what was the management fee compounding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tarudhan Valley (70 rooms) was terminated and Nestor (130 rooms, no fees) was removed, so fee-earning additions were lower. It said about 1,300 rooms were added year-on-year and that about 5,000 managed rooms signed in FY26 are due to open by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renovation timeline, and how much margin was lost to renovation versus GST and SAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renovation spend was Rs 9.8 crore (about 2.25-2.3% of revenue) versus a normal Rs 3 crore, and that about 300 rooms were done in Q1 with a similar number in Q2. It said refurbishments of about 800 rooms are planned in H2 and that the renovation drag disappears in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's acquisition push raise debt above 2x EBITDA, and how will the debt be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may briefly exceed 2x EBITDA during construction, with a long-term target near 2x. Fleur debt is about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; group debt is about Rs 1,275 crore after excluding about Rs 200 crore of cash. Warburg's Rs 960 crore will be deployed before listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Sharma said CCI approval is done and SEBI and exchange scrutiny is in progress, followed by NCLT filing and hearings. Completion is targeted in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in the late second half of calendar 2027 as the conservative assumption.

risks_watch: Q2 delivery versus management's claim that July was strong and August solid; the Q2 ARR recovery of 5-6% and the balance of negotiated versus non-negotiated business are unverified until the next print.
GST input-credit loss persists at about 2% of net revenue; the pace of pricing above Rs 7,500 (52% of room sales currently below) determines whether the drag falls as guided.
Mumbai and Gurgaon corporate demand softness and the roughly 2,000-room Mumbai airport supply overhang; Aurika Mumbai repricing may not translate into RevPAR growth.
Execution risk on the ~2,000-room FY27 opening target (334 opened in Q1) and on managed-hotel friction, including terminations that reduce net room additions.
Fleur capital deployment of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore and the debt-to-EBITDA path, plus demerger approvals (SEBI, shareholders, creditors, GST, NCLT) that could delay the H1 CY2027 completion.
Renovation spend and margin recovery depend on the H2 refurb schedule (about 800 rooms) and on FY28 margin of at least 50%, which management itself called a stretch if not achieved.
key_quotes: But I would say this is temporarily; this was undertaken largely to react to the swing to the situation that we had in Q1.
And there is no reason why our EBITDA margins net should be less than 50%.
We are not in an up cycle. We are not in an up cycle.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term margin and fee-income story and on Q2 recovery, but openly described Q1 as an aberration and said it was not happy with the quarter. It was guarded on giving numbers for Mumbai RevPAR and on capex, and it deferred several detailed questions to follow-up calls.
